target: new: two values of one bearer (dentated PATO_0001205 and lobed PATO_0001979)
reason: The part is lobed and its lobes are tooth-like, so both values hold together. The two values belong to different attributes (margin and division), so this is not a continuum. Same treatment as 'obliquely ovate'.

A shell-like exocarp or lemma is hard, thin and brittle like a nutshell, which is FLOPO crustaceous; its bearers already include fruit, lemma and bract. The shape reading (concave like a shell) is possible for bracts, hence medium.

target: new: two values of one bearer (undulate PATO_0000967 and serrated PATO_0001206)
reason: The margin is both wavy and serrate at once, so this is not a continuum between the two values. Both are stated of the same margin.
Absence of a part that has no term: 'appendage' and 'appendaged' were rejected as generic parts that need the organ they belong to (config/flora_rejected_bearer_words.tsv).
Fertile fern segments and pinnules bearing sporangia: PO sporangium (EXACT synonym sporangia) is present. 'Wholly' or 'entirely' is a coverage modifier and stays in RDF.
Loriform means strap-shaped. PATO_0002430 is 'shaped like a narrow band; ligulate'.

label: scutiform
definition: A shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being shaped like a shield: broad, rounded in outline and flat or slightly convex.
reason: No term exists. PATO_0002520 scute-like refers to an animal scute or osteoderm, and FLOPO:0991107 peltate is the attachment of a stalk, not the outline. Seeds, stigmas and leaves are described this way.

target: new: coloured lines (streaked FLOPO:0991206) with the colour of the lines (white PATO_0000323)
reason: The part is marked with white lines. 'White' is the colour of the lines, not of the part, so it cannot be a second value of the bearer. Streaked or striated is the marking, and the colour belongs to the lines.
Stems and branches 'with numerous leaf-scars' (French 'cicatrices foliaires'): the FLOPO anatomy class leaf scar is present. 'Prominent' or 'numerous' stay as modifiers.
Same as rule C204 lenticellate. 'Non lenticellés' is the same rule negated (lenticel absent). The 'lcnticcllés' OCR variant should be caught by the same cue.
A hyphenated compound of two outline shapes is a continuum between orbicular (PATO_0001934) and oblong (PATO_0000946), like 'ovate-lanceolate'.

target: new: part of the bearer (wall thickening, slot 1) + coiled (PATO_0000404)
reason: In moss peristome teeth it is the wall thickenings that run in a spiral, not the tooth itself. This needs a substituted bearer, as decided for 'thick-walled', not a new term.

label: straight-grained
definition: A structural quality inhering in wood by virtue of its axial elements (fibres and vessels) running parallel to the long axis of the stem.
reason: A standard wood-anatomy term with no PATO or FLOPO counterpart. Bearer: secondary xylem (PO_0005848).
Dithecous means two thecae: a count of 2 anther thecae (PO_0009069) on the anther. The suffix 'thecous' still has to be added to config/flora_counted_parts.tsv.
Semi-globular means half of a sphere: PATO_0005000 'A 3-D shape that is half of a sphere'.
A scape or inflorescence covered with bracts bears bracts. 'Densely covered' is a modifier. Same as rule C205 bracteate.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (place on the part, slot 1: margin) + brown (PATO_0000952)
reason: It is the margin that is brown, not the whole part. The value is stated of the margin region (PO margin class where one exists, else the BSPO margin region).
A continuum between elliptic (PATO_0000947) and orbicular (PATO_0001934), the second value qualified 'sub'.
In mosses 'border differentiated' only says that a leaf border is present, and 'narrowly' gives its width. Neither part has a term, and PATO_0002099 differentiated is a cell-type quality.
This is 'sub' plus julaceous (worm-like shoots with closely imbricate leaves), but there is no 'julaceous' term to qualify. A new base class for a few moss statements is too doubtful.

target: comparison or relation stated without its second term
reason: A comparative thickness of the wall without the cells it is compared with, as for rule C364 'thinner'.

target: new: two values of one bearer (erect PATO_0000622 and sinuous PATO_0001989)
reason: The awn or stem is upright overall and wavy along its length, so both values hold together. Flexuous maps to sinuous as in rule C318.
The negation of FLOPO excurrent, for a costa or vein that does not extend beyond the apex.
FLOPO:0991105 sheathing, weakened by the qualifier 'scarcely'. The degree stays in RDF.
Staminodes, stamens or a staminal tube 'portant des anthères' bear anthers, so anther is present. Where it says 'in its upper 2/3' is a region of the part.
Equal in length to another part (the calyx) is the equality case of the ratio-to-another-part pattern.
A gamosepalous calyx has its sepals fused to one another, which is connate (fusion of like parts), as for rule C171 'united'.
An alveolar receptacle or bract is honeycombed with close-set angular pits, which is FLOPO alveolate. The mesocarp case ('tissu alvéolé') reads the same.
Lageniform (French lagéniforme) means flask-shaped: swollen below and narrowed into a neck.
A pseudo-axillary inflorescence only seems axillary and actually arises outside the axil, which is FLOPO extra-axillary. Better than a new term.
